scope: Diagnoses the 2026-10-13 Mac-to-Strix bulk-transfer timeouts after the NVMe heatsink mitigation, separating the storage path from ZeroTier/TCP transport with host telemetry, packet captures, and disk-free rate tests.

attempts_over_mac_strix_zerotier.result: timed out after about 22 seconds; remote partial grew from 32768 to 65536 bytes
timed out after about 25 seconds; remote destination remained zero bytes

successful_control_path.description: The same 579789056-byte standard iMatrix was streamed from the main machine through the B550 SSH jump and then B550-to-Strix LAN relay.

unlimited.result: SSH timed out after the connection entered TCP retransmission; disk was not involved

disk_free_reproduction.interpretation: The failure has a narrow sustained-rate boundary between 64 and 128 KiB/s and is independent of NVMe reads or writes.

inner_tcp_summary.stall: The Mac repeatedly retransmitted sequence 292479:293667 while Strix repeated ACK 334059 with SACK; the Mac reset about 26 seconds later.

outer_udp_summary.recovery_behavior: At 2026-10-13T12:47:16Z Strix sent 137-byte UDP probes across nine local-port/remote-endpoint combinations before the Mac reset the TCP connection.

zerotier_state.both_peers_reported: DIRECT, but the selected IPv4 NAT endpoints changed repeatedly and the forward/reverse paths used different endpoint pairs.

diagnosis.leading: Rate-sensitive NAT/path renegotiation or packet-rate policing on the Mac-to-Strix ZeroTier IPv4 path. The endpoint changes, asymmetric UDP flows, TCP retransmission/SACK storm, and low-rate success make a host storage or SSH daemon defect unlikely.
diagnosis.confidence: High for transport-path cause; medium for whether the exact actor is CGNAT, either edge router, or ZeroTier 1.16.0/1.16.2 path selection.
diagnosis.why_now: This incident occurred during a sustained upload from the main machine to Strix. Earlier post-heatsink workloads were predominantly Strix reads polled over short command sessions, and the successful large transfer used a different Mac-to-B550 ZeroTier path followed by B550-to-Strix LAN relay.

checks.name: host-health
checks.result: same boot, watcher active, cool NVMe, zero D-state processes

checks.name: zerotier-peer-state
checks.result: both directions reported DIRECT through changing IPv4 endpoints

checks.name: packet-capture
commands: sudo systemd-run --unit=zt-inner-capture --collect tcpdump -i ztyjkdkgoy -s 256 -U -w /tmp/zt-inner-repro.pcap tcp port 22
checks.result: captured authenticated TCP stall and asymmetric ZeroTier UDP paths

checks.name: rate-boundary
checks.result: 64 KiB/s completed; 128 and 256 KiB/s timed out

checks.name: control-transfer
checks.command: cat standard-imatrix | ssh -J B550 Strix 'cat > temporary && sha256sum && mv'
checks.result: full 579789056-byte artifact and pinned SHA-256 verified

non_claims: This does not identify the exact ISP router, CGNAT node, firewall, or ZeroTier state machine that drops or re-keys the path.
Native IPv6 TCP to Strix timed out, so it could not serve as a control path; this likely reflects edge filtering but was not diagnosed further.
The temporary pcap files are not durable repository artifacts and may disappear on reboot; their hashes bind the analyzed copies at recording time.
No ZeroTier restart, interface MTU change, daemon upgrade, router change, or persistent route override was performed.
This finding does not generalize every Mac-to-Strix transfer; it explains the observed sustained-upload failures and gives the measured safe/control paths.
